title: Objection that God authors what he wills; reply: to will a thing in itself differs from willing its outcome
source_text: XXIX. Quod si quis objiciat Deum plane videri autorem eorum quae vult esse & fieri, quoniam voluntas Dei est causa rerum, respondent quod aliud est velle rem aliquam per se, aliud velle rem quoad eventum. Deinde quod Deus primo & proprie vult non impedire peccatum: & tantum ex consequenti vult eventum peccati: quia quod Deus non impedit, ideo evenit quia non impedit.
pass_a_gloss: XXIX. But if anyone object that God plainly seems the author of those things which he wills to be and be done, since the will of God is the cause of things, they answer that it is one thing to will a thing in itself, another to will a thing as to its event. Then that God first and properly wills not to hinder sin: and only consequently wills the event of sin: because what God does not hinder, therefore comes about because he does not hinder it.
pass_b_english: If someone objects that God plainly appears to be the author of what he wills to be and to be done, since God's will is the cause of things, they reply that willing a thing for its own sake is one thing and willing a thing as to its outcome is another.
They add that God first and properly wills not to hinder sin, and wills the outcome of sin only as a consequence. For what God does not hinder comes about precisely because he does not hinder it.
